solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Worry that the Queen's ignored duty

indicators.note: what the Queen owns is left out, so those letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: to exercise someone is to worry or trouble them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch fretting that her official duties were overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes ER (the Queen) from EXERCISE, which here means 'worry', as in a problem that exercises the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An excise is a tax or levy charged on goods, which is a kind of duty.

clue.text: Knight to open a centre rebuilt for access

indicators.note: the knight opens up the rearranged letters by going inside them
something rebuilt is put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight arriving to open a refurbished centre and give the public access.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges ACENTRE to ENTRACE; 'to open' puts N (knight, in chess) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is a way in, giving access to a building or place.

clue.text: False Tory attempted to take in Vatican leader

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: the letters take in, or swallow, another letter inside them

parts.note: attempted means tried

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dishonest Conservative trying to engage the Pope's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' places the Vatican's first letter inside the Tory-plus-attempted pair. 'False' sits at the front as the definition, not as a description of the Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contrived is forced and artificial, so it rings false.

clue.text: Be very angry if article is sat on by court

indicators.note: in a down answer the courting word sits on top of the article

parts.note: to see someone is to go out with or court them
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Fuming because a legal document has been ignored by a court.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is sat on by' puts SEE above THE. 'court' is a verb here, meaning to date.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil inwardly with rage, so it means being furious.

clue.text: It's a crop cultivated for fruit

indicators.note: land that is cultivated is worked over, so the letters of the phrase are dug over into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer explaining that a certain crop is grown for its fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges ITSACROP. The surface makes 'cultivated' a farming word, which hides it as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricots are small orange stone fruits, so they are an example of fruit.

clue.text: A real problem that Dracula might cause?

definitions.text: A real problem that Dracula might cause?

parts.words: A real problem that Dracula might cause?
parts.note: an idiom for a nuisance, read literally as the sore throat left by a vampire's bite

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an irritating person or thing, a real nuisance.

clue.text: Blow up stylish apartment with bit of explosive

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: a bit of a word is taken as its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone destroying a smart apartment with a small charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' looks like exploding, matching the surface, but it means fill with air.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate a balloon or tyre is to blow it up with air.

clue.text: I love to go around hugging chap from Muscat?

indicators.note: the reversed letters hug the chap between them
turning around reverses the order of the two letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone who loves going about embracing a man from the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go around' reverses I + O to OI, which then hugs MAN. Muscat is the capital of Oman.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital of Oman, so someone from there is Omani, the nationality adjective.

clue.text: A Rat? Bob Geldof could be described as one!

definitions.text: A Rat? Bob Geldof could be described as one!

parts.words: A Rat? Bob Geldof could be described as one!
parts.note: Geldof fronted the Irish band the Boomtown Rats as their lead vocalist

explanation.walkthrough: Bob Geldof, the organiser of Live Aid, was frontman of the Boomtown Rats, so a 'Rat' here is a member of that band.
explanation.definitionFit: Geldof was the lead vocalist of his band, so he is described as a vocalist.

clue.text: Rigid structures one might see on 10 down, I'm told

indicators.note: what someone has told you was heard spoken, so it signals a word that sounds like another

parts.words: structures one might see on 10 down
parts.note: tents are what you would see pitched on a camping ground, the answer to 10 down

explanation.surface: Someone passing on hearsay about stiff structures at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm told' signals a homophone: TENTS, said aloud, sounds like TENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense muscles or bodies are stiff and taut, so it is a synonym of rigid.

clue.text: Awfully nice hat I put over fellow's head

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A criticism of an ugly hat someone has perched on a man's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges NICEHATI together with F (fellow); 'put over' just links them. 'head' looks like part of the hat picture but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the leader of a clan or tribe, the head of the group.

clue.text: A place to pitch upcoming grand dances

indicators.note: letters that dance move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A venue being set up for some forthcoming big dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' rearranges UPCOMINGGRAND. 'pitch' means put up a tent, not a sports field or a sales talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A camping ground is a site where campers set up, or pitch, their tents.

clue.text: A poor actor will need support in Lincoln?

indicators.note: the actor phrase needs something put within it, so the support goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
a ham is an actor who overacts badly
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A weak performer needs propping up when appearing in a production in Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will need' puts the support inside A plus the poor actor. The question mark warns that Lincoln is an example: President Abraham Lincoln, not the English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham was the first name of the US president Lincoln, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: One publication that is covering new hit record

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mag is a magazine, a periodical publication

indicators.note: the that-is letters cover, or surround, the abbreviation for new

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A magazine featuring a story on a fresh chart-topping record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' wraps 'that is' round the letter for new. 'hit record' is the definition: a famous John Lennon single.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagine was John Lennon's famous 1971 song, a big-selling hit single.

clue.text: It's okay in Paris to have Spanish wine

definitions.meaning: the French phrase ça va means it's going fine or it's okay
a sparkling white wine from Catalonia

explanation.surface: A visitor to Paris approving of a glass of Spanish fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: The French ça va, written without its accent, gives the same letters as the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is the sparkling white wine of Spain, chiefly made in Catalonia.

clue.text: Insult bunch in shock to create this?

definitions.text: Insult bunch in shock to create this?

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for insulting them
a tress is a lock of hair, a bunch within a shock of hair

explanation.surface: Insults causing someone distress, the result of a deliberate slight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' here means a mass of hair, so a bunch in it is a TRESS. The whole clue also says that insulting someone causes this.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is the anguish or upset that hurtful insults are liable to provoke.

clue.text: Lascivious behaviour causes sin unfortunately

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A moralist warning that lewd conduct leads people into sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges CAUSESSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauciness is cheeky, sexually suggestive behaviour, a mild form of lasciviousness.

clue.text: Part of a yacht seen in seas as well as river

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the sea, so seas are mains
the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A sailor noticing a yacht fitting both out at sea and on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is a poetic word for the open sea. The TAY is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the stay, or supporting rope, running forward from the top of a sailing ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Animal crossing placard? I might create that!

indicators.note: the animal crosses, or goes around, the sign, so the sign sits inside

parts.note: a deer is an animal
a placard is a sign

explanation.surface: A road sign warning of animals crossing, and its proud creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' has the animal go round the placard. The surface suggests a deer-crossing road sign, and its maker is speaking as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer is the person who creates things such as signs and placards.

clue.text: Small problem with resistance leader in nick

indicators.note: the leading letter goes in, inside the word for a snag

parts.note: a catch is a hidden problem or snag

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A resistance chief in jail with a minor difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside CATCH, after S. 'nick' is British slang for prison, but here it is the definition, a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or notch, and so is a scratch.

clue.text: Young animal found near area in country

parts.note: a cub is the young of a bear, lion, fox and so on

explanation.surface: A young animal spotted near a particular area somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the Caribbean island nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Hit show originally about old Americans

indicators.note: the hit-and-show letters go about, round, the word for old

parts.note: to tan someone is to give them a beating
ex means former or old, as in an ex-wife

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the word gives only its first letter

explanation.surface: A popular TV show that started out about ancient Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the hit-plus-show letters round the word for old; 'originally' takes the first letter of 'show'. 'Hit' looks like a noun describing a show, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Texans are people from the US state of Texas, so they are Americans.

clue.text: Nasty chap that spies must detain or bug

indicators.note: the spies hold the man inside their letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents must either arrest a villain or plant a listening device on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must detain' puts the nasty chap inside the spies. 'bug' suggests a listening device, fitting the spy theme, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a loud chirping insect, and bug is an everyday word for an insect.

clue.text: Salesman and male tucking into eggs brought over for the boss?

indicators.note: brought over is a reversal for an answer written in a line, flipping the whole assembly backwards
the salesman and male tuck themselves inside the eggs

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman and another man eating eggs, served up for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' places salesman and male inside the eggs; 'brought over' then reverses the whole assembly. 'tucking into' looks like eating but places the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme ruler of an empire, the boss in a jokey sense.

clue.text: Simple idea containing bit of ingenuity

indicators.note: the idea word contains, or holds, the extra letter

parts.note: a plan is an idea for doing something

indicators.note: a bit of a word is taken as its first letter

explanation.surface: A straightforward idea that still shows some cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: I, from 'bit of ingenuity', goes inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unadorned and straightforward, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Treasonous speech missing introduction creates issue

indicators.note: losing its introduction means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: sedition is speech inciting rebellion against the state

explanation.surface: A rebel's speech, delivered without preamble, causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing introduction' takes the S off SEDITION. 'issue' means a printed number of a publication, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue of a newspaper or magazine, the copies printed at one time.

clue.text: One tight young man quickly earned cash

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
fast means tightly fixed, as in held fast
a buck is an old word for a dashing young man

explanation.surface: A stingy young man who made money in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like it means mean with money, which suits the surface, but it is FAST, as in 'stuck fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast buck is an idiom for money made quickly and easily, often shadily.

clue.text: High-ranking soldier punches vacuously abrupt spy

indicators.note: the soldier punches into, so goes inside, the emptied word
emptied of its contents, the word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for General, a senior army rank

explanation.surface: A general lashing out at a curt spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuously' empties 'abrupt' to its outside letters; 'punches' puts the soldier's abbreviation inside them. 'High-ranking soldier' is the general's short form, not a rank word in full.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone working secretly for an intelligence service, which is what a spy does.

clue.text: Use hands to sort out parasol?

indicators.note: sorting out a muddle rearranges things, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening up a tricky parasol by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sort out' rearranges USEHANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella held for shade from the sun, a type of sunshade.

clue.text: Swamp-like planet with hairy yeti-like leaders

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun

indicators.note: the leaders of the two following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A boggy alien world populated by shaggy creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes H and Y from 'hairy yeti-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is wet and boggy, so it resembles a swamp.
